idiom_name: AsyncStream per route (continuation.yield) plus an exhaustive switch over a sealed envelope enum
implementation_notes: Swift's concurrency model gives you the pieces but no router: model the message as an enum with associated values, hold one AsyncStream.Continuation per destination, and write the routing decision as a switch over the envelope that yields the value unchanged to the selected continuation. AsyncStream conforms to AsyncSequence, so each destination consumes with for await, the continuation is Sendable and may be called from concurrent contexts, and onTermination is where a route unsubscribes or tears down its source. The classic role objects (a rule table with named routes) are worth writing only when routes are installed at runtime from configuration; otherwise the enum switch plus a dictionary of continuations is the whole pattern and the routing function stays a pure, testable function.
pitfalls: AsyncStream buffers without limit by default (Int.max): pass a BufferingPolicy such as .bufferingNewest(n) or a stalled destination grows the process until it is killed.
The continuation must be finished and onTermination must cancel upstream work, otherwise the producer keeps running after the consumer stopped.
yield from an arbitrary thread is allowed because the continuation is Sendable, but shared route state still needs an actor or a lock to avoid data races.
finish() is terminal: a route that finished early cannot be reactivated, so routing mistakes surface as a permanently silent destination.
